item.description: The largest builders of artificial intelligence data centers have doubled their debt load in the last five years, turning to borrowing to finance an unprecedented spending spree they claim is needed to transform the economy.

item.title: Milky Mist Said to Launch $213 Million India IPO This Month
item.description: Milky Mist Dairy Food Ltd. is gearing up to launch its 20.35 billion rupees ($213 million) initial public offering as early as July, according to people familiar with the matter, paving the way for what is expected to be India’s largest dairy-sector IPO.

item.title: Traders Hedge for FX Volatility Return as Fed Uncertainty Builds
item.description: Currency traders are starting to buy protection against bigger exchange-rate swings after months of calm, as banks warn that shifting Federal Reserve expectations and elevated geopolitical tensions could be about to jolt markets.

item.title: South Africa’s Absa Faces Deeper Slide as Analysts Turn Cautious
item.description: A selloff in Absa Group Ltd. shares may have further to run as the South African lender’s disappointing earnings guidance causes once-bullish analysts to turn cautious on the stock.

item.title: Pfizer Vaccine Dispute Hits Polish, Romania Air Traffic Agencies
item.description: Poland and Romania’s legal battles with Pfizer Inc. over unused Covid-19 vaccine purchases are spilling into the funding of the eastern European nations’ air traffic agencies.

item.description: The European Union accused Meta Platforms Inc. of using addictive design and disregarding the risks it poses to children, as the bloc ramps up an investigation into the US social media company.

item.title: Spain’s Cuerpo Touts US Business Ties to Diffuse Trump Tensions
item.description: Spain is striving to strengthen business links with the US, despite tensions with Donald Trump, according to Economy and Trade Minister Carlos Cuerpo.

item.title: How Once-Struggling SK Hynix Became a Trillion-Dollar Company
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. is hardly a household name. But the maker of memory chips, which two decades ago was struggling to survive, is now South Korea’s second-most valuable listed company, just behind Samsung Electronics Co.

item.title: Web Scraper Sets $1 Million ‘Bug Bounty’ As Industry Scrutinized
item.description: Bright Data Ltd., an Israel-based startup that sells web scraping tools and datasets, is set to announce a $1 million “bug bounty” to root out bad actors as law enforcement steps up scrutiny of its industry.

item.title: Apollo Approaches Record Spend With EasyJet and Bayer Deals
item.description: Apollo Global Management Inc. is on course for a record year of acquisitions at a time when many of its private equity peers are struggling to deploy capital.

item.title: Cantor Opens Milan Office in Push to Land More European Deals
item.description: Cantor Fitzgerald LP is setting up an investment banking office in Milan and hired veteran banker Clarence Nahan to lead its expansion across Southern Europe, as the Wall Street firm sees untapped advisory opportunities in the region.

item.title: Cencosud Shares Tumble as Strategic Plan Yet to Boost Earnings
item.description: More than a year into a new strategic plan at Chile’s Cencosud SA, the retailer’s shares have slumped and the company is asking investors for patience.

item.title: BMW, Volkswagen Sales Decline on Worsening Slump in China
item.description: BMW AG and Volkswagen AG’s vehicle sales fell in the second quarter due to a worsening decline in China, where mounting competition from domestic rivals and a property crisis is stifling demand.

item.title: Spain’s Cuerpo Sees ‘Window of Opportunity’ for Joint EU Debt
item.description: Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo said he sees a chance to revisit the idea of joint borrowing within the European Union, despite initial skepticism to a proposal he made on the subject this week.

item.title: Nigeria Take Steps to Win Frontier Market Status as Stocks Surge
item.description: Nigeria is taking steps to ensure that its red-hot stock market wins a status upgrade by an influential index provider, as the West African nation seeks to capitalize on renewed investor interest.

item.title: SK Hynix ADR Allocation to Key Investors Said to Be Scaled Back
item.description: Key investors in SK Hynix Inc.’s $26.5 billion US listing received fewer American depositary receipts than initially anticipated, according to people familiar with the matter, as other buyers snapped up the deal.

item.title: Taiwan’s Population Slump Breaks Covid Record in Risk for AI Hub
item.description: Taiwan’s posted its longest stretch of population decline in data going back to the end of the second world war, underscoring the demographic challenges facing the manufacturing hub at the center of the global AI boom.

item.title: UAE’s Oil Output Surged to Record High in June, IEA Says
item.description: The United Arab Emirates boosted crude oil production to an all-time high last month, the most compelling evidence yet of how Abu Dhabi responded more boldly than any of its Persian Gulf neighbors to disruption caused by the Iran war.

item.title: SoftBank Names Ex-Goldman Sachs Trader Agne to Lead Vision Fund Finances
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. has picked former Goldman Sachs trader Mark Agne to oversee finance and technology at the Vision Fund, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Vanguard Buys Inflation-Protected Bonds on an Oil-Market Oddity
item.description: Unusual moves in an oil-market gauge are prompting Vanguard Asset Management Ltd. to buy insurance against stickier-than-expected US inflation.

item.title: India Power Giant Seeks Uranium Assets Overseas in Nuclear Push
item.description: India’s largest power producer is seeking to invest in overseas uranium mines to secure supplies needed to fuel 30 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity it plans to build over the next two decades.

item.title: EU Banks Urged to Pool Buying Power in Deals With US Tech Giants
item.description: Banks and finance firms should combine their buying power to avoid losing out in negotiations with US tech giants, according to raft of Dutch proposals aimed at tackling Europe’s over-dependence on foreign providers of critical services such as AI and cloud computing.
